**SUBJECT: Urgent Pre-Service Clinical Appeal**
*   **Member Name:** Sawyer Delgado
*   **Member ID:** W188500611
*   **Reference Number:** POC-C3B5D8F398-85355
*   **Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030)
*   **Provider:** Lindqvist, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)
*   **Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-13

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my lower back disc surgery and decompression (CPT code 63030), which was recommended by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist. 

Your denial letter dated August 13, 2026, states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." Under Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield's governing policy—specifically the Carelon Medical Benefits Management *Musculoskeletal Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Doc ID: MSK03-1125.1-UC0126)—this decision is clinically incorrect. My clinical presentation, physical examination, imaging results, and exhaustive history of conservative treatment directly satisfy all applicable medical-necessity criteria for an "Initial disc herniation".

Below, I map my medical records to the clinical guidelines to demonstrate that this procedure is indeed medically necessary.

### 1. Objective Correlation of Advanced Imaging Findings
The clinical guidelines state that there must be:
> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings."
> "The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

My advanced imaging findings are as follows:
*   **Lumbar Spine MRI (Dated 2026-06-30):** This study demonstrates an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. 

This MRI was performed within the last two months (well within the required 6-month window) and confirms objective, severe structural compression of the neural pathways. 

### 2. Clinical Correlation and Objective Physical Exam Findings
The clinical guidelines permit surgery for an:
> "Initial disc herniation when ALL the following criteria are met: Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as: Nerve root tension sign, Dermatomal sensory loss, Motor strength deficit (myotomal), Abnormal reflex"

My symptoms and physical exam findings perfectly correlate with the L4-L5 disc extrusion imaged on June 30, 2026:
*   **Radicular Pain & Distribution:** I experience severe, progressive radicular pain radiating directly into my right calf, which corresponds clinically to the compressed right L5 nerve root.
*   **Physical Exam Findings:** Dr. Lindqvist's physical exam documented positive provocative testing (nerve root tension signs) on the affected right side, along with a focal neurological deficit that maps directly to the L4-L5 level.
*   **Significant Functional Impairment:** Due to this nerve compression, my physical function is severely limited; I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time. This severely restricts my basic activities of daily living (ADLs).

### 3. Exhaustive Trial of Conservative Management
The governing guidelines require a:
> "Lack of improvement or resolution after completing at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (such as physical therapy, activity modification, or pharmacotherapy)."

I have undergone 9 months of progressive lower back pain, during which I fully exhausted and failed conservative treatment protocols:
*   **Supervised Physical Therapy:** I completed a 10-week course of formal, supervised physical therapy (focusing on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility) from April 10, 2026, to June 19, 2026. This comprised 24 total visits, as fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note. 
*   **Pharmacotherapy:** I used prescribed NSAIDs for 4 months, which failed to provide adequate pain relief.
*   **Interventional Management:** On April 14, 2026, I received a lumbar corticosteroid injection, which provided only 3 weeks of partial, temporary relief before my severe symptoms returned.

### Summary of Clinical Fit
My condition is not self-limiting or responsive to non-surgical care. I have severe radiculopathy, matching objective physical exam findings, and an MRI from June 30, 2026, confirming a corresponding L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis. I have completed 10 weeks of physical therapy and 4 months of medication with zero long-term resolution. 

I meet every standard of medical necessity set forth by your plan's Carelon clinical guidelines. I strongly request that you review the attached physical therapy records, physician clinical notes, and the radiologist’s report for the June 30, 2026 MRI, and immediately reverse this denial. 

Please contact Dr. Lindqvist’s office at [Doctor's Phone Number] or myself at [Patient Phone Number] if you require any additional information to expedite this authorization.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Delgado
